Petitioner :- Ayub @ Buba And 7 Others
Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 2 Others

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Ajay Nand Pandey Hon'ble Vivek Kumar Birla,J.
Hon'ble Surendra Singh-I,J.
Heard Sri Ram Raj Pandey, learned counsel for the petitioners, Sri Ajay Nand Pandey, learned counsel for the informant and Ms. Manju Thakur, learned A.G.A for the State respondents.

The relief sought in this petition is for quashing of the F.I.R. dated 12.03.2023 registered as Case Crime No.243 of 2023 under Sections 307, 323, 504, 498A IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act and Section 3/4 Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019, Police Station Baghpat, District Baghpat.

entities.text: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Further prayer has been made not to arrest the petitioners in the aforesaid case.

Submission of the learned counsel for the petitioners is that only on the basis of general allegations the entire family has been roped in; the allegation regarding Triple Talak is also false and the Ayub @ Buba And 7 Others vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13112538/
1 injuries are simple in nature.

entities.text: Ayub @ Buba And 7 Others vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submits that the there is every possibility of peaceful compromise in the present case.

It is next submitted that the impugned first information report is nothing but a malicious prosecution only to harass the entire family wherein distinct relations and old persons of the family have also been implicated.

Per contra, learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for quashing of the FIR and submits that earlier the mediation has taken place but the same got failed and there is no scope of further mediation.
Learned counsel for the informant further submits that the victim has suffered various injuries including the injuries on the vital part i.e. head injury.
This fact has been disclosed in the first information report itself.

Learned AGA also supports the argument of the learned counsel for the informant and submits that it is case where injuries have been suffered which were duly examined in the Community Health Centre, therefore, a cognizable offence has been made out.
Perusal of the impugned first information report prima facie reveals commission of cognizable offence.

Therefore, in view of the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana and others vs. Bhajan Lal and others, 1992 Supp. (1) SCC 335 and M/s Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt.
Ltd. vs. State of Maharashtra, AIR 2021 SC 1918 and in Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No.3262/2021 (Leelavati Devi @ Leelawati & another vs. the State of Uttar Pradesh) decided on 07.10.2021, no case has been made out for interference with the impugned first information report.
